speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe exactly where you feel the pain in your wrist and hand, and what specific movements are difficult for you to perform?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's tenosynovitis. Your history of a fall on an outstretched hand six months ago likely caused an initial injury or strain that has now resulted in chronic inflammation and tendonitis affecting the tendons on the thumb side of your wrist. The pain radiating to the elbow and worsening with holding your infant son are classic symptoms of this condition. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out other causes, I would like to perform a physical exam known as Finkelstein's test, which involves having you make a fist with your thumb tucked inside and then bending your wrist toward your pinky finger. If this test reproduces the pain you're feeling, it will strongly support the diagnosis of De Quervain's tenosynovitis. Additionally, an ultrasound or MRI may be useful if the condition does not respond to conservative treatment or if there is concern for a more serious underlying issue.
